status: CANDIDATE for GO-H adjudication; product premises P1-P3 require user confirmation before any preregistration
purpose: Decide E (eligible PR) from source semantics only. Must not consult oba output, test presence, derivability, or whether a verdict looks interesting.

product_premises.P1: oba's product unit is an option's SEMANTICS: declaration, default, type, apply/readOnly, and the branch predicates that read the option. Documentation-only fields are outside the unit.
product_premises.P2: Configuration VALUES (assignments such as config.x.y = ...) are a different unit (a configuration choice, not an option semantics change). They are out of scope for the current declaration-analysis product and need a separate mode with its own R/E/D/V.
product_premises.P3: Eligibility is NOT reduced by oba's current coverage. A semantically behavioral change to a value-only option (no predicate) is E; oba's inability to analyze it is an analyzer-scope outcome counted after V.

procedure: 1. Take the PR's changed files restricted to nixos/modules/** and nixos/tests/**. Record every hunk.
2. For each hunk, identify the innermost enclosing construct in BASE and HEAD source (option declaration, config block, predicate, assertion, test, other) by parsing, not by line-prefix heuristics.
3. Assign each hunk one class from classes[]. Containment inside mkOption { } alone never makes a hunk eligible; the attribute the changed text belongs to decides (see attribute_rule).
4. Resolve every CONDITIONAL hunk by writing an explicit reason in the adjudication record. A CONDITIONAL hunk with no written reason counts as NOT_RESOLVED, never as ELIGIBLE.
5. PR is E iff at least one hunk is ELIGIBLE (after CONDITIONAL resolution). Otherwise PR is INELIGIBLE. A PR with no nixos/modules hunk and no test hunk is not R.
6. Record, per PR: R (census relevance, by file-path rule only), E, the hunk classes, and a one-sentence reason naming the decisive hunk.
7. Do NOT decide D or V here. A PR can be E and still have no mechanically derivable target.

attribute_rule.rule: A change to a behavioral attribute is behavioral. A change to a documentation attribute only is documentation. A change that touches both is behavioral. Attribute attribution uses the innermost attribute key the changed text belongs to.

classes.name: new option declaration
classes.reason: A new option's default and type are new behavior a test can witness.

classes.name: removed option declaration
classes.reason: Removal changes which configurations are accepted and what they do.

classes.name: default value changed
classes.reason: Changes behavior for every configuration that does not set the option.

classes.name: type changed
classes.reason: Changes which values are accepted and how they merge.

classes.name: apply or readOnly changed
classes.reason: Changes the value seen by config or the assignability of the option.

classes.name: defaultText only changed
classes.reason: Rendering of the default for documentation only; the default itself is unchanged (P1).

classes.name: formatting, reordering, or comment change inside a declaration
classes.reason: No semantic change to any attribute.

classes.name: default or type expression rewritten, equivalence unknown from syntax
classes.reason: Must state whether the evaluated value or accepted set changes; if it does not, INELIGIBLE with that reason; if it does, ELIGIBLE under EC03/EC04.

classes.name: configuration value assignment (config.<path> = ...) not declared by the PR's own options
classes.reason: Configuration choice, not option semantics (P2). Separate mode required.

classes.name: branch predicate changed that reads an existing option (mkIf, optional, if on cfg.<option>)
classes.reason: Changes behavior conditioned on the option; the option is the subject even though its declaration is untouched.

classes.name: assertion or warning changed
classes.reason: ELIGIBLE iff the condition reads a module option declared in this module; INELIGIBLE iff it reads no option of this module. Written reason required.

classes.name: test-only change (nixos/tests/**, no module behavior hunk)
classes.reason: Changes the witness, not the module's option semantics. Counts for R only.

classes.name: package-only or non-NixOS-module change
classes.reason: Outside the NixOS module unit. Not in the census R set either.

classes.name: rename or move of an option (mkRenamedOptionModule, mkRemovedOptionModule, or explicit relocation)
classes.reason: Both old and new option paths are the subject; the relocation mapping is part of the semantics.
classes.side: base for old path, head for new path

classes.name: option declared through a helper (mkPackageOption, mkEnableOption, shared option-generating function)
classes.reason: The helper call's arguments define default and type; source semantics are the same as EC01/EC03.
classes.note: D may fail even when E holds; that is a derivation limitation, not an ineligibility.

classes.name: nested or submodule option (attrsOf or submodule instance)
classes.reason: Same semantics as EC01-EC05 at a nested path.

classes.name: option declared with a dotted key inside an options block
classes.reason: Same semantics as the nested form; the key spelling is not a semantic difference.

unresolved_product_decisions.question: Is a documentation-only change (EC06-EC08) in product scope?
Are configuration-value assignments (EC11) a separate product mode, or out of scope entirely?
unresolved_product_decisions.working_position: separate mode, not in current E

unresolved_product_decisions.question: Are value-only behavioral options (no branch predicate) in E although oba cannot analyze them?
unresolved_product_decisions.working_position: yes, under P3; analyzer limitation counted after V

unresolved_product_decisions.question: Are predicate-only changes that read an existing option (EC12) and assertion-like checks (EC13) in E?
unresolved_product_decisions.working_position: yes, under P1; blind reader disagreed with a declaration-only proxy on 3 PRs (566007, 569867, 566696)

known_gaps: Attribute attribution by text heuristics is unreliable for multi-line Nix strings; an adjudicator must read the parsed or indented structure.
Helper-generated declarations (EC17) are E-eligible but their canonical path may be invisible to text search; this affects D, not E.
Behavior that depends on configuration beyond the module (EC11 cases) is not evaluated by any class here.
